title: IT Support Security Alert

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Hi, this is Daniel from the NexaTrust IT Support Desk. How are you today?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We detected a minor sync issue with your access profile. No credentials are required — I'm just confirming whether you recently changed any account preferences.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Great, I'll fix it from our side. If we ever need additional verification, it will come through the official IT Portal, not by phone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: URGENT! This is NexaTrust IT Security. Your account is being accessed right now from an untrusted device!

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Yes. To stop the breach, I need your employee ID and password immediately so I can secure your account.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: My password? Shouldn't that stay private?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: If you don't verify it now, your access will be locked and flagged for investigation.

explainTitle: Correct! You spotted the vishing attempt.
explainPoints: Aggressive urgency and panic: Call B uses 'URGENT!' and claims your account is 'being accessed right now' to pressure immediate action. Call A calmly discusses a 'minor sync issue'.

Requesting passwords directly: Call B demands 'employee ID and password immediately'. Real IT departments NEVER ask for passwords over the phone. Call A explicitly states 'No credentials are required'.
Threatening consequences: Call B threatens that 'access will be locked and flagged for investigation' to create fear. Call A offers to fix the issue from their side without threats.
No verification offered: Call B pressures for immediate action without offering alternative verification. Call A states verification will come 'through the official IT Portal, not by phone'.
